---
title: "Named indexes twin"
filters:
  - index
---

The core shapes of `named-indexes.qmd` — the same terms, targets, sort key and
range — written by a document that declares no indexes at all and names none on
any mark. It is the shape a declaration leaves untouched: one index, headed
`Index`, under the section id this extension has always minted, with every
judgement made across the whole document because the whole document is one
index.

A mark that names no index: [Aardvark]{.index}. A second one:
[Babbage]{.index}.

One term, marked twice, with a sort key on one of the marks:
[Hague]{.index sort="Zebra"} and [Hague]{.index}. One entry, filed under Z.

Both cross-references resolve here, because both targets are in the one index:
[near]{.index entry="Neighbour" see="Aardvark"} and
[far]{.index entry="Stranger" see="Aardvark"}.

The range pairs here, because both of its marks are in the one index:
[Cantor]{.index range="open"} opens it and [Cantor]{.index range="close"}
closes it.
